assumptions_resolved: Round 1 of the governed review (head a5dba125) returned REVISE. Five IDENTITY evasions and two fail-open paths were closed; the activation window and the settled-not-relevant limit were recorded in the config instead, because closing the first would require editing a merged migration and the second is a judgement a regex cannot make.

Round 2 (head 21bfe963) returned REVISE. The two fail-open paths that turned the guard into a silent no-op (unvalidated activation_migration, absent migrations directory) now refuse; schema detection no longer depends on literal spelling; the removal direction covers drop column/table/schema; comment and header parsing is a scanner rather than a line regex; and a row that shouts both a settled and an open marker reads OPEN. The owner-ruling citation form remains a shape check and is now documented as one.

Generation 1 assumed the guard would ship as its own workflow file. pr-guards.yml carries the newer, more specific convention that a repo-wide guard is a job there. The job moved, the standalone workflow was deleted, and the check-run name is unchanged so no required context changes.

A new script under scripts/ requires a reviewed throughput-disposition catalogue; generation 1 did not allow that path, so Tools offline tests refused. The catalogue is added with a written disposition for each of the three comment lines that match the tracked pattern.
Every check above was re-run at this exact commit. Earlier reports cited runs at earlier SHAs, which round 2 correctly refused as unbound evidence.

Round 3 (head 24844be6) returned REVISE with two fail-opens in the guard itself. H1: dollar-quoted bodies were blanked before the identity and schema tests, so an identity constraint asserted or dropped inside a DO block or a function body was never tested and the check went green. Bodies are now scanned AS SQL, recursively, so their own comments and strings are still excluded. H2: header detection compared raw and stripped text line by line, and blanking a multi-line construct shortened the stripped side; the drift refused genuine headers and accepted fake ones. Header positions now come from one offset-returning scan. H3, H4, M1, M2, M4, L1 and L2 are also fixed in code. Each has a negative test.

H4 was fixed by scoping the settled decision to the register row STATUS cell rather than by widening the open-marker veto row-wide. The wide version was implemented first and it read the real register entry 2.36 as OPEN: that entry states the identity question is ANSWERED and, in the same cell, that a separate cost sub-question is still open. A row-wide case-insensitive veto would therefore refuse every citation of a correctly answered entry. The real-register test caught it.
